title: UFO Moviez India Ltd - 539141 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: UFO Moviez Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose to ₹1,299 million (+17% YoY) but EBITDA was flat at ₹213 million and PAT fell to ₹64 million.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 17% YoY to ₹1,299 million in Q2 FY27, driven by higher product-sale revenue from equipment sales, while EBITDA was broadly flat YoY at ₹213 million (vs ₹218 million) and net profit fell to ₹64 million from ₹75 million. H1 FY27 revenue rose 10% to ₹2,417 million, but H1 EBITDA (₹402 million) and PAT (₹121 million) were both lower YoY. Management attributed the margin squeeze mainly to a ~₹1 crore rise in variable incentive accrual and a 66% jump in equipment cost of goods sold, and guided to stronger Q3 and Q4 on a film slate of sequels and tentpole releases. Analyst questions focused on cost structure, operating leverage, promoter holding and dividend/buyback capacity.

segments.name: Advertising
segments.commentary: Advertising revenue share costs rose only 2% YoY; management says services ad margin is above 55%. Ad revenue growth was not quantified for the quarter.

segments.name: VPF and Digital Cinema Network (CDC)
segments.commentary: VPF revenue share costs rose 16% YoY, in line with VPF revenue; management cites a 60-65% margin for VPF plus CDC services.

segments.name: Sale of equipment/products
segments.commentary: Product revenue rose 66% YoY to ₹422 million with a net margin up 68%; management puts historical product gross margin at 18-24% over about 20 quarters.

guidance_outlook: No revenue number committed for Q3 or Q4 FY27; management said advertisers are buying across film bunches and that the next two quarters should be better than the trailing quarters.
Management said no cost surprises are expected in Q3 and Q4, with costs budgeted and the incentive accrual already rationalised.
Board discussions on a capital distribution policy (dividend or buyback) are underway; management expects clarity by Q3 or Q4 FY27, not a payout for the current year.

Management said operating leverage should kick in at current ad and service revenue levels; illustrative ₹6 crore of extra ad revenue at ~70% PBT margin would lift PBT by ~₹4.2 crore (45-50%) from the reported ₹9.6 crore PBT.
capex_capacity: Advertising footprint at 3,946 screens: 2,606 multiplex and 1,340 single screens.
Releases in Q2 FY27: 386 movies including versions/languages, vs 462 in Q2 FY26 and 399 in Q1 FY27.
Capex, capacity utilisation and commissioning timelines were not discussed on the call.
demand_pricing: Q2 film performance was mixed: Spider-Man: Brand New Day, Hanuman Ansh (sleeper hit), Awarapan 2 and Mirzapur: The Movie did well; Alpha, Batwara 1947, Toxic, Haiwaan underperformed.
Q3 FY27 started with Drishyam 3, Jailer 2, Udta Teer and Prahaar; upcoming slate includes Ramayana Part 1, King, Avengers: Doomsday, Eetha, Yeh Prem Mol Liya and Godzilla.
Advertisers are willing to commit to bunches of films rather than film-by-film, per management.
Management said Q3 and Q4 FY26 benefited from Dhurandhar, so the comparison base is tougher.

qa_highlights.question: How much accumulated losses remain, and can the company pay a dividend or buyback given its cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the ~₹119 crore accumulated losses are tax losses held as a deferred tax asset. Companies Act losses were removed through a NCLT-approved share capital reduction about two years ago, so dividends and buybacks are permitted. A capital distribution policy is being discussed at board level, with an update expected in Q3 or Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Promoter holding has been falling; will promoters raise their stake?
qa_highlights.answer: The fall is due to Apollo International being reclassified as non-promoter after depromoterisation in Q4 FY26, not promoter selling. Founder group (Valuable Technologies, Sanjay Gaikwad, Hete) stake is intact. Any increase is the promoters' decision; no indication has been given.

qa_highlights.question: Why did direct costs rise sharply and why did profit growth lag revenue growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said operating direct costs rose 28% YoY, mostly from COGS on equipment sales (+66%), which was matched by product revenue (+66% to ₹422 million). EBITDA fell 2% YoY because the variable incentive accrual rose about ₹1 crore and fixed salary and SG&A increased. Excluding the incentive, EBITDA would be up about 2%.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company quantify the operating leverage threshold, and are there further cost cuts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave an illustration: ₹6 crore of additional ad revenue at a 70% PBT margin would add about ₹4.2 crore to the reported ₹9.6 crore PBT. It said major manpower and SG&A cuts were made about 2.5 years ago and that further cost-cutting is not the focus.

qa_highlights.question: Can management give a Q3 advertising revenue range, and are there cost surprises ahead?
qa_highlights.answer: Siddharth Bhardwaj declined to give a revenue number, citing no past practice, but said Q3 and H2 should beat expectations on the film slate. Asked for above ₹400 million per quarter, he did not confirm it. Ashish Malushte said there would be no cost surprises and costs are budgeted.

risks_watch: EBITDA margin compression: EBITDA margin fell as revenue grew 17% while EBITDA grew only about 2%; watch whether the product-sales mix keeps diluting margins.
Content dependence: several highly anticipated Q2 titles (Toxic, Batwara 1947, Haiwaan) underperformed, and management acknowledged audience selectivity.
Q3 and Q4 depend on the release slate (Ramayana Part 1, King, Avengers: Doomsday) and on advertisers committing to film bunches; no revenue guidance was given.
Dividend or buyback policy: timing is set for Q3 or Q4 FY27, and the board has not decided.
Management's statement that Q2 revenue was ₹1,118 million compared with Q1 FY27 conflicts with the ₹1,299 million Q2 figure, so the QoQ comparison needs verification against the filing.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the demand outlook and cost discipline, but evasive on specific Q3 and Q4 revenue numbers. Management was defensive when pressed on the margin decline and attributed it to incentive accrual and product-mix effects.
key_quotes: So the current reported 9.6 crores PBT would have gone up by 4.2 crores, so almost 45-50% increase in my PBT.
So we would refrain from committing a revenue number because we have never done this in the past.
And that is the accumulated losses that actually stands in my balance sheet in the form of a deferred tax asset.
There are not going to be any surprises when you see the revenues going up.

growth.why: No numeric revenue guidance for Q3/Q4 FY27; management only said the next two quarters should be better than trailing quarters, with advertisers committing to film bunches, and no capacity additions, capex or utilisation were discussed, so the outlook rests on the film slate rather than capacity or orders.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA was flat at ₹213m in Q2 (-2% YoY) on revenue +17%, and management says operating leverage kicks in at current ad levels (₹6 crore extra ad revenue at ~70% PBT margin would add ~₹4.2 crore to ₹9.6 crore PBT), but product sales at 18-24% gross margin dilute the mix and incentive accrual was rationalised rather than cut.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Capex, capacity utilisation and commissioning timelines were not discussed; the footprint is 3,946 screens with no new capacity announced.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Releases were 386 in Q2 FY27 vs 462 in Q2 FY26 (down ~16%), so volume depends on the Q3-Q4 slate (Ramayana Part 1, King, Avengers: Doomsday) and advertisers buying film bunches; Q3-Q4 FY26 comparison is tougher due to Dhurandhar.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed; the asset-light ad model has no utilisation metric given, and the ₹1,657m cash balance is being considered for a capital distribution policy rather than capex.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management said Q3 and H2 should beat expectations on the film slate and that the next two quarters should be better than trailing quarters, but declined to give a numeric Q3 revenue range even when pressed for above ₹400m per quarter.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management said no cost surprises are expected in Q3 and Q4 with costs budgeted and the incentive accrual already rationalised, though Q2 titles Toxic, Batwara 1947 and Haiwaan underperformed.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product, brand or model launches were discussed; the equipment sales line is an existing business.

rows.label: Dividend or buyback policy decision
rows.why: Board is discussing a capital distribution policy with an update expected in Q3 or Q4 FY27, against ₹1,657m consolidated cash and ₹865m net cash; no payout is expected for the current year.

rows.label: Ad bunch commitments from advertisers
rows.why: Advertisers are willing to commit to film bunches rather than film-by-film, but no committed ad revenue figure was given for Q3 or Q4.

rows.label: Variable incentive accrual reset
rows.why: The ~₹1 crore rise in variable incentive accrual that cut Q2 EBITDA has been rationalised, and excluding it EBITDA would be up about 2% YoY.

tone.note: Management was confident on the film slate, cost budgets and the capital distribution policy, but declined to give a Q3 revenue number and was defensive on the 2% EBITDA decline; analysts pushed on margins, operating leverage, promoter holding and payout capacity.
